source_text.ISS-0937:
id: ISS-0937
title: "Backend CI red at UTC month boundary: TenantTemplateTest parity (extra events_y2026m09) and PartitionMaintenance/RetentionOperations/EventRetention tests ({:error,:partition_not_eligible}) fail on 2026-10-01"
discovered_by: ELIXIR-DEV
discovered_in_run: WF03-ISS0930-20261001 (Step Final, PR #2076; filed by ORCH)
discovered_at: "2026-10-01T00:21:56Z"
severity: MAJOR
description: >
  PR #2076 (scripts/fixtures-only, no lib/ or migration change) had its backend job fail twice. Run 1: one TenantTemplateTest
  parity failure extra=["events_y2026m09"]. Re-run after the 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01 UTC rollover: 12 failures in
  PartitionMaintenanceTest, RetentionOperationsTest, EventRetentionTest ({:error, :partition_not_eligible}). Hypothesis, not
  reproduced on main: the tests depend on the real current UTC month / partition eligibility and break at the month boundary.
  PR #2076 was merged with --admin per decision 0018. Confirm via main's CI on ed40c2fa, then make the tests clock-independent.
affected_files:
  - test/letflow/events/ (partition maintenance / retention tests)
  - test/letflow/tenants/ (tenant template parity test)
queue_ref: Q-920  # queue issue_ref ISS-0920 collides with an existing local file; local filename ISS-0937
github_ref: GH-2077
status: open

task.description: WF-03 Step 3d REVIEWER gate for ISS-0937. Review git diff origin/main..HEAD (non-handoff files) against the validated design lib/letflow/design/iss0937-month-boundary-test-clock.md: scope creep (only test/support + the three retention tests; lib/ and migrations untouched - verify with git diff --stat), consistency with decision records in docs/migration/decisions/ (esp. any on test isolation / partition retention / tenant template), idiomatic Elixir (module naming Letflow.Test.PartitionClock, @spec, no process-global state, helper pure, wrappers delegate), whether the design's non-blocking notes from step-02b were honoured, correctness of the offset rule yourself (do arithmetic for several dates), and the claim that retention tests now pass on the 1st (you may re-run the three retention test files in the worktree; DB via .env; deps already present). Verdict PASS/FAIL with concrete defects. Modify nothing but this handoff. Set IN_PROGRESS at claim then COMPLETED/FAILED, result.status PASS/FAIL; next_action 'Route to TEST-DESIGNER' on PASS.

result.summary: No scope creep: lib/ and priv/ diff is only the design doc; test changes confined to test/support (partition_clock.ex new, tenant_template.ex, tenant_fixture.ex adding dynamic predicate) and the three retention tests. No decision-record conflict (0037 partition retention untouched; no record on test clock). Idiom OK: Letflow.Test.PartitionClock pure, @spec, guard, no process/global state, never reads clock; wrappers delegate with @override_age_days single source; single regex retained in TenantFixture. Offset rule M=shift(month(today-N),-1) hand-verified: N=1: 2026-10-01->08, 10-02->09, 10-31->09, 2027-01-01->11, 2028-03-01->2028-01; N=31 on 10-01->07 (Aug cutoff Oct 2 ineligible). Step-02b notes honoured (dynamic-only filter on both sides, fixed tables retained, comment corrected, moduledoc formula fixed, fingerprint unchanged). Re-ran the three retention test files on the real date 2026-10-01 (the 1st): 31 tests, 0 failures. Non-blocking: the design's fail-first tests (partition_clock_test.exs, ISS-0937 describe in tenant_template_test.exs) are absent from the diff; they must be written by TEST-DESIGNER. Local current_month/shift_months copies retained per design. No type-safety issue filed.
